rationale: Evaluation shows quality pass but rejection (paired_gain_not_above_noise, objective_not_improved): candidate ttft 28.107 ms vs paired parent 25.037 ms. Two uncorroborated uncertainties remain: (1) the candidate-declared route 'parent_fallback_setup_failure' (count 2) with binding effective 'direct' and 'no functional replacements' is candidate-reported telemetry that interpretation explicitly asks to corroborate with traces or actual exception evidence; (2) the source of the ~3 ms TTFT regression is unknown and must not be assumed to be algorithm cost, since the declared fallback implies the parent path executed and the delta could be setup-failure handling, binding-layer overhead, or noise. Selections on this exact candidate in separate workers: candidate_diagnostics to capture the actual setup-failure exception/stack behind the declared fallback route; execution_timeline for a plain trace with CPU-to-CUDA submit associations and synchronization intervals around the prefill-to-first-token boundary to attribute host-side gaps vs GPU work and corroborate the executed code path (noting GPU readiness/consumer completion may remain unknown); binding_cost because an additive candidate exists and did not replace the parent (effective direct, parent_fallback route), giving clean AB/BA parent vs binding-only passthrough whole-invocation cost with quality checks to test whether the regression is binding overhead; nsys is available (request.json tools.nsys) and useful for the attribution question, independently resolving whether the TTFT delta sits in host gaps between CUDA submissions or in kernel durations, which execution_timeline alone cannot fully bound. torch already ran (coverage: 66441/66441 kernels associated, 0 ambiguous). nccl_tuning and collective_calibration are not applicable (single device, no NCCL); device_telemetry's device-wide native sampling windows cannot resolve a ~25-30 ms prefill interval attribution; python_runtime is excluded because its perturbation would confound a small delta and host dispatch attribution is covered by execution_timeline plus binding_cost.
